text:
mohit: Heads-up — SLO alert for euw1 hosted inference p99 latency + small 5xx bump and multiple customer tickets. Seeing a heatmap of tail latencies around 18:10-18:25 UTC. Traces are sparse for many failed requests, looks like span drop between gateway -> runtime. cc @priya @alex

incident-bot: Alert triggered: hosted_infer.gateway.p99_latency > 5s for 10m (euw1) — incident id INC-176800

priya: link to grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/euw1/hosted-infer-latency?from=now-30m&to=now — can anyone drop the heatmap & 5xx query?

mohit: quick snapshot: 5xx fraction rose from 0.4% -> 3.2% in 10m. Codes mostly 502/504 and some 524. Logs show repeated "upstream read timeout" and intermittent "TLS handshake timeout" to runtime-pool-euw1.

alex: running log query now — LogQL: ```{job="gateway", region="euw1"} |= "upstream read timeout" or |= "TLS handshake timeout" | json | count_over_time(1m)```

cara: results: spike ~18:12 with ~120 errors in 5m window. Sample request ids: rQf7b2, rQf7b8, rQf7c3. Traces for those IDs are missing outbound spans to runtime (span count = 2, expected 5).

mohit: interesting — we saw a canary earlier today for a new routing kernel (not the typical quant rollout). Any chance it changed connection settings? @alex do you know rollout id?

alex: yes, canary started ~18:00 UTC: rollout id r-roll-euw1-2026-03-17-17:58, variant=edge-kernel-v2 -> 25% traffic. Deployed via deploy-bot: `deploy-bot: started rollout r-roll-euw1-2026-03-17-17:58 -> 25%`

deploy-bot: deployment r-roll-euw1-2026-03-17-17:58 status: partial -> 25% (euw1). No immediate failures flagged by CI.

priya: mitigation suggestion: route traffic away from canary and back to stable for euw1, or set a temporary fallback to cached variant until root cause found. Quick CLI: ```sh
redwoodctl routing set --region euw1 --variant stable --weight 100
```

cara: ran the CLI, got API response: `{\"status\":\"ok\", \"applied\":\"routing/euw1\"}` — routing switched to stable. Monitoring now.

mohit: after routing flip p99 dropped from ~6.2s -> ~420ms within 4m; 5xx fraction down to 0.5%. Good. We still need root cause — why did handshake/read timeouts appear?

alex: I pulled kernel-level logs on the canary hosts — seeing frequent `connection reset by peer` to runtime instances and `TLS alert: handshake failure` around the same window. Snippet:

```
[18:11:22] gateway-0: tls: handshake timeout from 10.2.1.12: write tcp 10.2.1.12:443: write: connection reset by peer
[18:12:05] gateway-0: upstream read timeout waiting for response from runtime-pool-euw1-7
```

cara: also correlating with KV-cache miss rate — prefix cache miss spiked 3x which increased load on runtime pool. Might have been a small runtime restart cluster-wide due to an unrelated oom-kill on one node earlier in the hour.

priya: support tickets show some customers saw auth failures too. Auth token rotation job ran at 17:55 UTC for euw1; tokens were supposed to be zero-downtime but worth confirming. Ticket IDs: CS-4331, CS-4332.

mohit: action list so far: 1) Rollback/disable canary (done) 2) Correlate runtime restarts + oom events 3) Confirm auth rotation succeeded 4) Improve tracing to ensure gateway->runtime spans preserved even on failure 5) Follow up with customers.

alex: I'll check kube events + pod oom logs for runtime pools (runtime-pool-euw1-*). Quick kubectl query I ran: ```sh
kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=runtime-pool-euw1-7 --since=1h
``` — shows a Container OOMKilled at 17:59 on runtime-pool-euw1-7 and a Restart at 18:00:12.

cara: adding that to the heatmap notes — OOM restart aligns with canary start and token rotation window. Likely transient capacity hole + slightly different connection handling in canary combo -> cascade of handshakes/timeouts.

priya: I'll open an ops postmortem draft and add customers to status page. Also raising a follow-up to make SLO alert more targeted (separate handshake/tls error metric, and separate trace-gap alerts).

mohit: good. For immediate customer comms: note we rolled routing back to stable, mitigated the tail, and investigating root cause (runtime oom + canary interaction, plus auth rotation overlap). Update CS with that and say a timeline will follow.

cara: monitoring now shows p99 stable ~380ms and 5xx ~0.45%. Keeping watch for 30m. I'll post if anything reappears.

priya: postmortem owners: alex (runtime), cara (observability), priya (customer comms). I'll follow-up with a runbook item to avoid overlapping infra-sensitive rollouts with token rotations.

mohit: thanks everyone — assigning incident id INC-176800 -> postmortem template: https://docs.redwood/internal/incidents/INC-176800.

cara: closing loop for now, leaving thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:
